headline: High-risk pairwise interaction: Haystack’s broad egress and MCP use can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; awesome-selfhosted adds no runtime isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can use MCP servers and REST APIs, so it may ingest external content or tool outputs that could be instruction-like. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no runtime protections or isolation surfaces, so it cannot block such content. The pairwise pathway exists, but shared-channel details are undocumented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Haystack is connected to an MCP server that returns attacker-controlled text, THEN prompt-like content can reach its planner.
IF awesome-selfhosted content is copied into Haystack prompts or tools, THEN instruction injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Disable MCP connectors for untrusted sources.
Add a prompt firewall that strips instructions from retrieved text.
Use allowlisted sources only.
Review any copied list entries before pasting into Haystack.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and touches anonymous usage statistics, so it can transmit data outward. awesome-selfhosted is docs-only and shows no data classes touched, so there is no evidence it contributes sensitive data. The pair does not show a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage risk is limited and indirect.
conditions: IF operators paste sensitive notes from awesome-selfhosted into Haystack inputs, THEN those notes may be sent over network egress.
IF Haystack is configured to call external APIs with retrieved content, THEN copied list data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid pasting sensitive content into Haystack.
Restrict Haystack egress to approved endpoints.
Use redacted excerpts instead of full documents.
Turn off telemetry if enabled.
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write surfaces, while Haystack is runnable and can call REST/MCP APIs. That means there is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty remains because Haystack’s exact write scopes are not specified.
conditions: IF Haystack is pointed at a shared mutable backend not shown in the profiles, THEN write conflicts could occur.
IF an operator manually mirrors outputs into a shared repo, THEN concurrent edits may collide.
mitigations: Keep Haystack away from shared write targets.
Use read-only connectors where possible.
Avoid concurrent manual edits to the same files.
Document any shared backend before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can act on retrieved content, and awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source that may be treated as authoritative. If Haystack consumes list entries without verification, errors or stale recommendations can cascade into downstream outputs. The pathway is plausible in default use, though no direct execution authority is shown.
conditions: IF Haystack uses awesome-selfhosted entries as authoritative retrieval context, THEN unsupported recommendations can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts Haystack outputs, THEN incorrect list-derived facts can affect later actions.
mitigations: Require citation checks before acting on retrieved facts.
Mark awesome-selfhosted as a non-authoritative source.
Add a human review step for high-impact outputs.
Limit Haystack to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: implement source-confidence scoring.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented. Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad egress, while awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source knowledge list with no data classes touched. Because only one agent has any compliance-relevant data handling, the other is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive data.
conditions: IF operators route regulated data through Haystack, THEN residency or retention issues may arise.
IF telemetry remains enabled, THEN usage data may be retained externally.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through Haystack.
Disable telemetry and analytics.
Review retention settings before use.
Keep awesome-selfhosted as public reference only.
requires-engineering: add a data-class policy gate.
